---
title: "Parameterization in BayesIRTplot"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(BayesIRTplot)
```

This article provides details on the parameterization of item response theory (IRT) models fitted in `blavaan`, and explains how those parameters are transformed and used for plotting in `BayesIRTplot`.

IRT models are fitted in `blavaan` using the theta parameterization and a probit link (i.e., the normal-ogive model). For a unidimensional two-parameter IRT model, `blavaan` provides posterior draws of item discrimination (`a`) and item threshold (`tau`) parameters. `BayesIRTplot` applies the following transformations and calculations:

1. Under the normal-ogive model, the probability of a correct response (`p`) is calculated as the probability that the underlying latent response exceeds the item threshold.
2. Item discrimination (`a`) is converted from the probit to the logit metric using $$
a_{\text{logit}} = 1.702a_{\text{probit}}
$$ and is reported under the logit metric. 
3. Item information (`i`) is calculated as $$
i = a_{\text{logit}}^2 p(1-p)
$$.
4. Item threshold (`tau`) is not transformed and is reported under the original probit metric.
